answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 17 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The sable multiplier is published, charged in cipher, and dawn lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 1774 identities would post 4575 proofs and burn roughly 43 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
